text:
Research supports joint semantic–collaborative learning, but the retrieved papers do not establish the exact combination of BERT4Rec, title/description encoding from scratch, and fine-grained attribute contrastive learning. [CLA-Rec (ICDM 2024)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10884256/) aligns description embeddings with collaborative representations through contrastive learning, then models sequences with a Transformer; its reliance on pretrained LLM embeddings makes it unsuitable unchanged. [Q-BERT4Rec (December 2025; revised March 2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.02474) combines semantic injection, residual quantization, and multiple masking strategies, but includes visual/structural features and does not establish the requested text-only, from-scratch setting.

An older, directly relevant foundation is [Recformer (KDD 2023)](https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~jmcauley/pdfs/kdd23b.pdf): it identifies coarse sentence representations and separately trained language/recommendation components as limitations, motivating word-level attribute modeling and joint objectives. Its architecture is not a drop-in BERT4Rec replacement. [Kim et al. (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.18667) additionally report benefits from jointly learning interaction signals and description-based item contrastive objectives, although their knowledge-graph setting differs from this benchmark.

Experimental inference: retain BERT4Rec and add a small randomly initialized token encoder with separate title/description field embeddings and attentive pooling. Jointly learn gated fusion with item-ID embeddings using masked-item loss plus a modest same-item ID–text alignment loss. Preserve model numbers, dimensions, and negation during tokenization; avoid treating broad textual similarity as proof of interchangeability. At masked positions, hide both target ID and target text. Use appended-mask inference and one checkpoint per category. This is a testable adaptation, not a literature-established improvement; text alone cannot establish ownership or exact compatibility.
